subject: SRE readiness: SIEM audit exporter SLOs + alerting + beta on-call expectations
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Apr 8, 2025 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: SRE readiness: SIEM audit exporter SLOs + alerting + beta on-call expectations

Priya — sharing SRE’s proposal for SLOs/alerts + what we’ll page on during the SIEM audit export beta.

Assumptions (beta):
- At-least-once delivery + downstream dedup expected (per delivery semantics ADR)
- Exporter can auto-pause per destination on sustained downstream failures (feature-flagged)
- Beta cohort is 3–5 tenants; we’re OK with “ticket-first” for some conditions as long as security-impacting issues page.

Proposed SLOs (beta) — per destination + per tenant:
1) Export lag (p95): 15 minutes over a 24h window
   - lag = now - newest successfully delivered event timestamp (by destination checkpoint)
2) Delivery success rate: 99.5% over 24h
   - success measured at batch level (HTTP 2xx for Splunk/Datadog, successful write + checkpoint persist for S3)
3) Exporter availability: 99.9% (process + queue consumption + checkpoint writes)

Alerting / paging policy (beta):
P0 page (SRE on-call):
- lag p95 > 60 minutes for a single destination for >= 30 minutes (sustained)
- exporter not making progress (checkpoint age increasing) for >= 15 minutes across >2 beta tenants
- DLQ growth rate > X (suggest: > 500 events/min) for >= 10 minutes OR DLQ size > 1M events (whichever hits first)
- config fetch failures from control plane for >= 10 minutes (all tenants) OR auth failures after rotation attempt

P1 ticket (no page, unless customer escalation):
- adapter 429s sustained but lag < 60 min and exporter is backing off as expected
- per-destination error rate > 1% for >= 60 minutes but lag < 60 min

What we need from you + PM/Sec/Compliance:
- Confirm “lag” definition is acceptable for beta customer expectations (Naomi/Olga)
- Confirm whether any conditions above should be treated as security incidents (Marcus)
- Confirm we’re comfortable with the p95 15m target for beta vs tighter (Priya)

I’ll post the draft SLO/alert page + dashboard links once the panels are finalized today.

Thanks,
Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Apr 8, 2025 at 10:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: SRE readiness: SIEM audit exporter SLOs + alerting + beta on-call expectations

This looks directionally good.

Two questions:
1) For beta, can we bias more toward “ticket-first” unless it’s a full stop? I want to avoid noisy paging while we’re still tuning backpressure (esp. Splunk 429s).
2) Do we have a single dashboard that consolidates: lag, retries/backoff, checkpoint age, and per-adapter error codes? (So on-call isn’t hopping between 5 panels.)

Also please include a clear “when to pause exports” criterion + who has permission to do it (SRE vs Support vs Security).

Priya



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Apr 8, 2025 at 11:18 AM PDT
Subject: Re: SRE readiness: SIEM audit exporter SLOs + alerting + beta on-call expectations

Agree on “ticket-first” for expected downstream throttling.

Updates based on your note:

Paging changes (beta):
- Keep pages for “no progress” / checkpoint stall, control plane config fetch failures, or broad impact (multiple beta tenants).
- Move “lag p95 > 60m for a single destination” to ticket-first IF:
  a) errors are dominated by 429/5xx from destination AND
  b) exporter backoff is engaged AND
  c) max lag safety hasn’t triggered (auto-pause)
- Page only if max lag safety triggers OR lag > 4 hours sustained (single destination) OR customer escalates.

Dashboard: now live (still adding 2 panels):
https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/audit-exporter/audit-exporter-overview?orgId=1
Includes:
- Export lag by destination (p50/p95) + checkpoint age
- Delivery success rate (2xx / non-2xx) by adapter
- Retry/backoff counters and current backoff window
- DLQ size + ingress rate
- “Auto-paused destinations” table

Runbook draft (WIP but usable):
https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Runbook+-+Audit+Exporter+Delivery+Failures

Pause criteria + permissions (proposal):
- Auto-pause: exporter triggers when lag > 4h OR consecutive failures > N (default 50) for a destination.
- Manual pause: SRE on-call can pause/resume per destination per tenant.
- Support: can request pause via INT ticket; no direct action in beta.
- Security: can request immediate pause if exfil risk is suspected.

Naomi/Olga — can you confirm that “4h max lag safety => exporter auto-pauses” is acceptable language for beta expectations? (We can tune threshold; I’m proposing it mainly as a blast-radius limiter.)

Neha



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Apr 8, 2025 at 12:07 PM PDT
Subject: Re: SRE readiness: SIEM audit exporter SLOs + alerting + beta on-call expectations

This is helpful.

For customer-facing beta expectations, I’d like to avoid promising a specific max lag (esp. since the customer’s SIEM can throttle us).

Can we frame it as:
- “near-real-time under normal conditions”
- “delays possible during downstream throttling/outages; exporter retries with backoff and provides delivery status/health”
- “customers should deduplicate by event_id”

Also: if we auto-pause at 4h, what’s the recovery story? Do we automatically resume when destination recovers, or require manual resume? We should be explicit for weekly beta check-ins.

Naomi



From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Apr 8, 2025 at 12:29 PM PDT
Subject: Re: SRE readiness: SIEM audit exporter SLOs + alerting + beta on-call expectations

+1 to Naomi’s framing.

Two security-specific notes for the alerting/runbook:
1) Please ensure we don’t log destination credentials (HEC token, Datadog API key, IAM role ARN session creds) in exporter logs. If an auth failure occurs, we should log only the destination ID + a reason code.
2) Some conditions should be treated as security incidents (page + engage SecEng) even if delivery is still “working,” e.g.:
   - egress allowlist violation / destination host validation failure that looks like attempted exfil
   - unexpected destination changes (config churn) outside approved RBAC role
   - repeated 403/401 after “successful” secret rotation attempts (possible compromised or mis-scoped keys)

Olga — we should align on evidence language: Redwood provides delivery status and attempts; customer retains SIEM-side retention responsibilities.

Marcus



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 10, 2025 at 4:41 PM PDT
Subject: Re: SRE readiness: SIEM audit exporter SLOs + alerting + beta on-call expectations

Closing the loop with proposed wording + final beta paging expectations. (Will also paste into PM-858 readiness checklist.)

Customer-facing (beta) wording suggestion (for FAQ / check-ins):
- Redwood audit export is designed for continuous delivery with at-least-once semantics.
- Under normal operating conditions, events are delivered near-real-time.
- During downstream throttling or outages, delivery may be delayed; the exporter will retry with backoff and expose delivery health and lag in the Console.
- Customers should deduplicate using event_id.

Auto-pause / recovery:
- Auto-pause triggers as a safety mechanism if a destination is failing and lag exceeds the configured max-lag threshold.
- In beta we will NOT auto-resume by default; resume is manual (SRE) after destination validation.
  Rationale: avoids flapping + prevents accidental duplication storms when a destination comes back with partial acceptance.

Paging expectations (beta):
- Page SRE on-call for:
  1) exporter no-progress / checkpoint stall across multiple beta tenants
  2) control plane config fetch failures or config corruption symptoms
  3) security-relevant signals (egress allowlist violations, suspicious auth patterns) — per Marcus’ notes
  4) customer escalation on perceived missing events (we’ll use dashboard + runbook + DLQ tooling)
- Ticket-first for:
  - sustained 429s / destination-side throttling while backoff is engaged and checkpoint is progressing (even slowly)

Action items:
- Neha: incorporate Marcus’ logging guidance into runbook (and confirm exporter logs are redacted) by EOW.
- Olga: confirm evidence language for SOC2 questionnaires (retention vs export responsibilities).
- Priya/Naomi: thumbs-up on the beta SLO targets (15m p95 lag / 99.5% delivery) as INTERNAL goals only.

Links (unchanged):
- SLO/alert draft: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Audit+Exporter+SLOs+%26+Alerting+(Beta)
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Runbook+-+Audit+Exporter+Delivery+Failures
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/audit-exporter/audit-exporter-overview?orgId=1

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
